tieu_de: Coober Pedy: Why People Dig Their Bedrooms
mo_ta_dong: Coober Pedy is an opal-mining town in the outback of South Australia, and estimates vary, but around half of it lives in homes dug into the hills. Wob went there to move in, melted by noon, and found out why people here dig instead of build.

Opal found by a teenager in 1915, leftover dirt piles everywhere, rock that ignores the weather, a truck that vacuums out bedrooms, golf with no grass, water piped from a distant bore, old mine shafts, and the country of the Antakirinja Matu-Yankunytjatjara people.

Kanku-Breakaways is a registered Aboriginal heritage site owned by the Antakirinja Matu-Yankunytjatjara Aboriginal Corporation. If you visit, please don't touch or take anything. And please don't go noodling at night: old mine shafts are often unmarked.
